around.headline: Fake currency racket busted in Bengaluru: seven held, 4.3k notes seized
around.summary: Police broke a counterfeit-note racket and seized about 4,300 notes. Check security features on notes received as change, especially in crowded shops, markets and festival stalls.

around.headline: Pink Line elevated section set for safety inspection Oct 6–8
around.summary: The Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety is likely to inspect the 7.5-km elevated stretch, which would take Namma Metro past 100 km. Inspection is a step before opening; no opening date has been reported.

around.headline: Bike ambulances launched at Bengaluru traffic hotspots
around.summary: Emergency first responders on two-wheelers have been launched, including a service by Manipal Hospitals, to reach patients faster through traffic. In an emergency, still call 108 or 112 first.

around.headline: Can meter autos make a comeback? Commuters face unregulated charges
around.summary: Deccan Herald looks at why meters are losing ground and what that means for fares. Agree the fare or book through an app before you get in, and note the vehicle number.

around.headline: East Bengaluru road projects fast-tracked, junction promised within 15–20 days
around.summary: Officials say pending road works on the east side are being sped up, with one junction promised within 15–20 days. Commuters in that belt may see diversions while work is on.

around.headline: 2BHK for Rs 70,000 rent and Rs 4 lakh deposit sparks debate
around.summary: A viral listing has reopened the debate on Bengaluru's high rental deposits. Get a written agreement and receipts for any deposit, and ask exactly when and how it is refunded.

around.headline: Sensex falls 571 points on Oct 1 as auto stocks drag markets
around.summary: The Nifty slipped 0.88%. Daily swings like this matter little for long-term SIP investors; avoid panic selling.

street_smart.title: A shopkeeper at a crowded stall hands you change, and one Rs 500 note feels slightly too smooth and the thread looks printed rather than embedded. You only notice after you've walked a few steps away. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Times of India, Oct 2: 'Fake currency racket busted: Seven held, 4.3k notes seized in Bengaluru'.
street_smart.situation: You're not sure the note is fake, but several things about it look off, and you're tempted to just get rid of it.

choices.text: Quietly spend it at the next busy shop so you don't lose Rs 500.
choices.feedback: Once you suspect a note is fake, passing it on makes you part of the chain. Counterfeit notes survive precisely because each victim hands them on to the next person, and knowingly doing so is a criminal offence.

choices.text: Tear it up or throw it away and say nothing.
choices.feedback: You lose the money and the evidence. A fake note you destroy can't help the bank or police trace where it came from.

choices.text: Go back at once and loudly accuse the shopkeeper of cheating you.
choices.feedback: The shopkeeper may be an unknowing victim too, and a public confrontation can turn ugly. If the shop is the source, calm evidence works better than shouting.

choices.text: Check the watermark, security thread and feel against a genuine note, stop using it, note where you got it, and take it to your bank branch or the police.
choices.feedback: Comparing against a genuine note tells you if it's real, and the printed-not-embedded thread is a classic giveaway. Handing it to the bank gets it removed from circulation, and your note of the source helps trace the racket.

takeaways: Compare any doubtful note with a genuine one: watermark, embedded security thread and raised print.
Never knowingly pass on a suspected fake note; take it to a bank branch or the police.
Count your change before leaving the counter, especially in festival crowds and at night.

quiz.question: How many people were held in the fake currency racket busted in Bengaluru, as reported by TOI?
quiz.why: About 4,300 counterfeit notes were seized. Genuine notes carry a colour-shifting security thread and a watermark.

quiz.question: Which Vande Bharat service did the Railway Minister say will be extended to Bengaluru?
quiz.why: The service currently links Goa and coastal Karnataka; no start date for the Bengaluru extension was reported.

quiz.question: By roughly how much did the Nifty slip on Oct 1?
quiz.why: The Sensex fell 571 points on the day. Nifty is the NSE index of 50 large companies; Sensex tracks 30 on the BSE.

quiz.question: Gandhi Jayanti, observed on Oct 2, marks Mahatma Gandhi's birth in which city?
quiz.why: Born in 1869, Gandhi's birthday is also observed internationally as the International Day of Non-Violence.

quiz.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution protects the right to life and personal liberty?
quiz.why: Courts have read many rights into Article 21, including privacy and a clean environment.
